Welcome to Sparsholt Church of England Primary School. If you are exploring schools for your child, we hope this website helps you discover the warmth, ambition and Christian ethos that makes our village school such a wonderful place to learn and grow.
Headteacher’s Welcome – Mrs Gemma Cutler
All our staff, children, parents, carers and Governors are incredibly proud of Sparsholt Church of England Primary School. As the Headteacher, it is a privilege to lead this warm, nurturing and forward‑looking village school. We believe deeply in the partnership between home and school and are committed to building a shared responsibility for your child’s education, wellbeing and spiritual development.
Our core Christian values of Courage, Compassion and Creativity lie at the centre of our community and shape everything we do. These Christian values, rooted in the teachings of the bible, guide our children as they grow in character, kindness and resilience. They underpin our vision for every pupil to flourish in mind, body and spirit.
Sparsholt’s beautiful rural location contributes greatly to our distinctiveness. Set in the heart of a thriving village, we benefit from a close relationship with St Stephen’s Church, located just opposite the school. The church is a natural extension of our learning environment: we visit regularly for worship, celebrations, special services and curriculum‑linked activities that deepen pupils’ understanding of faith, community and belonging. We also welcome children from beyond our immediate catchment, with bus services available for families living further afield, helping ensure our school community is inclusive and accessible. Our newly developed pond and forest area enhances our outdoor learning offer, supporting our commitment to providing children with meaningful experiences in nature. As part of our growing outdoor learning initiative, all pupils enjoy curriculum time in these beautiful spaces — developing curiosity, environmental responsibility, wellbeing and a deep connection to the natural world.
Sparsholt is also recognised for the strength of its ethos and the quality of its provision. Our most recent SIAMS inspection graded the school as EXCELLENT, describing Sparsholt as “a truly inspiring place to learn and work” and celebrating how our Christian vision is lived out with authenticity and kindness, enabling pupils and adults to flourish. In our 2023 Ofsted inspection, the school was judged Outstanding for both Behaviour and Attitudes and Personal Development, with inspectors noting our welcoming atmosphere, exemplary conduct and the impressive leadership shown by our older pupils. These affirmations reflect the distinctive strength and character of our community.
Building on this strong foundation, we offer a vibrant and ambitious curriculum that ignites curiosity and celebrates children’s talents. At Sparsholt, learning goes far beyond the statutory requirements: we believe children benefit from a full, varied and enriched curriculum that broadens their horizons and allows them to discover their passions. Teachers plan rich, well‑sequenced learning experiences — enhanced by opportunities in sport, music, outdoor learning, creative arts and technology — ensuring every child is inspired, challenged and supported to achieve their very best. Our commitment is not only to help children achieve academically, but also to nurture their confidence, creativity, spirituality and love of learning.
Thank you for taking the time to visit our website. If you are considering Sparsholt for your child, I warmly encourage you to come and see the school in action. A visit will give you a true sense of our caring ethos, our lively classrooms and the strong Christian values that underpin daily life here. Please contact the school office to book a tour — we would be delighted to welcome you.

What is the Sports Premium Grant?
The Sports Premium Grant is additional funding from the Government to improve provision of physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools.
It is also for improving the health and wellbeing of all primary pupils.
At Sparsholt C of E Primary School we aim to ensure that every child has equal access to a wide range of sporting activities, both competitive and non-competitive, and that physical activity is promoted to encourage high levels of participation throughout the school. The school wishes to ensure that children’s engagement is long lasting and to celebrate and encourage participation that continues beyond the vicinity of the school.
The School Governors are committed to closely monitoring the spending and impact of the Sports Premium through the revision at the Curriculum Committee.

Many children may experience some difficulty in their learning at some time during their education. Often Quality First Inclusive Teaching will mean that most children overcome their difficulties quickly and easily. pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium Overview
The Pupil Premium was introduced in April 2011 and paid to local authorities by a grant based on the number of pupils registered as eligible for free school meals (FSM) in Reception to Year 11. Schools decide how the Pupil Premium is spent, since it is recognised that they are best placed to assess what additional provision should be made for the individual pupils within their responsibility. The Pupil Premium Grant is currently (2024-25) £1480 per child.
From April 2012, the Government widened the coverage of the Premium to include those eligible for FSM at any point in the previous six years (known as the Ever 6 FSM measure).
Parents can now check eligibility for Free School Meals using the easy online facility which has been launched by Hampshire County Council Catering Services (HC3S). This self-service option is available at:
Hampshire County Council Free School Meals Eligibility & Information
This online service requires your name, National Insurance number or Asylum number, address and child’s name, date of birth and school. If your child is eligible for FSM the system automatically tells the school. The school can also help you with the online service; just come to the school office with the information required as detailed above.
The Service Children Premium is currently (2023-24) £340 per child. This is to support emotional and social well-being. The Service Children premium is for pupils with one of their parents serving in the regular armed forces (including pupils with a parent who is on full commitment as part of the full time reserve), one of their parents died whilst serving in the armed forces and the pupil receives a pension under the Armed Forces Compensation Scheme or the War Pensions Scheme, or a pupil who has been registered as a ‘service child’ on the January school census at any point since 2015.
For more details on the Pupil Premium and Service Premium visit the Schools, Colleges, and Children's Service Website:
Support for Children & Young People - Pupil Premium & Service Premium

What is the Sports Premium Grant?
The Sports Premium Grant is additional funding from the Government to improve provision of physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools.
It is also for improving the health and wellbeing of all primary pupils.
At Sparsholt C of E Primary School we aim to ensure that every child has equal access to a wide range of sporting activities, both competitive and non-competitive, and that physical activity is promoted to encourage high levels of participation throughout the school. The school wishes to ensure that children’s engagement is long lasting and to celebrate and encourage participation that continues beyond the vicinity of the school.
The School Governors are committed to closely monitoring the spending and impact of the Sports Premium through the revision at the Curriculum Committee.

Wraparound Childcare
School-Run Breakfast Club
As wraparound childcare, we offer a Breakfast Club for Yr R through to Yr 6 pupils, Monday to Friday from 8:00am to 8:40am during term time. This club is operated and staffed by the School.

How are we enhancing provision further?
At Sparsholt we have enhanced our provision further by introducing specific school sports earlier. Our Year 1 children now have access to a range of after-school activities and we have purchased the correct equipment to enable younger children to play lacrosse.
We aim for children to build their lacrosse skills progressively from a young age, becoming talented team players. We have also secured further specialist coaching time to provide experienced instruction for the younger pupils.
We also continue to strengthen the skills of our Year 5 and 6 Sports Leaders, providing opportunities for them to run sports clubs, support PE lessons and organise whole school events (under the supervision of the class teacher).
We have also created our own Sparsholt Shooting Stars award scheme which encourages, recognises and rewards physical activity both in and outside of school. The children also undertake the Sparsholt Stride which aims for all children to have completed at least 5km a week of 'striding' around the school grounds. This is a safe, simple and measurable health & physical activity initiative accessible to all our children regardless of ability. We aim to inspire and encourage the children with a focus on fun, rewarding personal achievement, as well as raising money and healthy competition.

Pupil Premium Overview
The Pupil Premium was introduced in April 2011 and paid to local authorities by a grant based on the number of pupils registered as eligible for free school meals (FSM) in Reception to Year 11. Schools decide how the Pupil Premium is spent, since it is recognised that they are best placed to assess what additional provision should be made for the individual pupils within their responsibility. The Pupil Premium Grant is currently (2024-25) £1480 per child.
From April 2012, the Government widened the coverage of the Premium to include those eligible for FSM at any point in the previous six years (known as the Ever 6 FSM measure).
Parents can now check eligibility for Free School Meals using the easy online facility which has been launched by Hampshire County Council Catering Services (HC3S). This self-service option is available at:
Hampshire County Council Free School Meals Eligibility & Information
This online service requires your name, National Insurance number or Asylum number, address and child’s name, date of birth and school. If your child is eligible for FSM the system automatically tells the school. The school can also help you with the online service; just come to the school office with the information required as detailed above.
The Service Children Premium is currently (2023-24) £340 per child. This is to support emotional and social well-being. The Service Children premium is for pupils with one of their parents serving in the regular armed forces (including pupils with a parent who is on full commitment as part of the full time reserve), one of their parents died whilst serving in the armed forces and the pupil receives a pension under the Armed Forces Compensation Scheme or the War Pensions Scheme, or a pupil who has been registered as a ‘service child’ on the January school census at any point since 2015.
For more details on the Pupil Premium and Service Premium visit the Schools, Colleges, and Children's Service Website:
Support for Children & Young People - Pupil Premium & Service Premium
